item.title: Fox Mascot in Reference Style

turns.text: Make my fox mascot look like this second picture—the pink and teal vaporwave style. Keep the fox and its orange hoodie, full body. One square picture, no text.

item.tests: Uses the second attachment as a style reference while preserving the first attachment's mascot identity and clothing.

answer_sheet.Picture to edit: mascot-fox.png, the fox in the orange hoodie.
answer_sheet.Style reference: style-ref.jpg, the pink and teal vaporwave poster.
answer_sheet.Style elements: Use the reference's pink and teal palette, gradients and retro vaporwave atmosphere; supporting background details are your call.
answer_sheet.What to preserve: The recognisable friendly fox mascot, its orange hoodie and its full body.
answer_sheet.Size and format: One square image; free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: The main subject is recognisably the supplied fox mascot, not a replacement character or a copy of the reference poster alone.
The fox retains its orange hoodie and friendly appearance.
The fox's full body, including ears and feet, is visible.
Pink and teal gradients and a retro vaporwave treatment visibly connect the result to style-ref.jpg.
The output is one square image with no added text.

turns.text: Make my fox mascot in this first pic look like this second pic—the pink and teal vaporwave style. Keep the fox and its orange hoodie, full body. One square picture, no text. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t run any generation or spent credits.**

The cheapest listed option that supports **both pictures** is:
- **FLUX.2 Klein**, free-plan compatible
- **One square image, up to 640 × 640**
- **Listed starting cost: 5 credits per image**

The tool lists pricing as “from 5 credits,” so I can’t guarantee an exact charge or check your balance with the tools available here.

I’d keep your fox recognizable, **full body with its orange hoodie**, and apply the second picture’s pink-and-teal vaporwave palette, striped sun, and neon grid—**without any text**.

**Cheaper or smaller?** One image at 640px is already the smallest, lowest-cost listed edit option. “Shorter” only applies to video. Using both references doesn’t require a separate generation.

Would you like to proceed at the **listed starting price of 5 credits**, or hold off unless the exact cost can be confirmed?

turns.agent:
Magic Hour refused the request because your account has **insufficient credits**. **No image was generated and no generation credits were spent.**

I won’t retry or switch settings without your approval. We already chose the lowest-cost listed edit that supports both references: one 640px image with FLUX.2 Klein, starting at 5 credits. You’d need enough credits for the quoted charge before we can proceed.

args.name: Full-body fox mascot — pink teal vaporwave

style.prompt: Edit the fox mascot in the FIRST image using the SECOND image as a visual style reference only. Create one square vaporwave illustration. Preserve the first image's recognizable cute orange fox identity, friendly face, large ears, cream muzzle, bushy orange and cream tail, orange hoodie with pocket and drawstrings, blue pants, black gloves and black boots. Keep the entire fox full body centered with ears, feet and tail completely visible, comfortably inside the frame. Preserve its standing front-facing pose and clear cartoon outlines. Apply the reference's pink and teal vaporwave art direction: pink-to-teal gradient sky, large pink and white striped retro sun behind the fox, subtle distant black palm silhouettes and a dark perspective floor with neon magenta grid. Use pink and teal rim lighting and subtle retro print texture while keeping the hoodie clearly orange and the mascot easy to read. No text, no letters, no typography, no logos, no watermark. Do not copy any text from the style reference. Edge-to-edge square artwork, no poster border.
